source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a function of the skin?
questions.rationale: Skin protects, regulates temperature, senses, secretes, excretes, limits water loss, and produces vitamin D.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Skin functions (PDF p. 446)
questions.quote: It produces and absorbs vitamin D.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a skin biopsy, the client should be told that sutures are usually removed in:
questions.rationale: Keep the dressing on at least 8 hours, watch for bleeding and infection, and return for suture removal in 7–10 days.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Skin biopsy (PDF p. 446)
questions.quote: Sutures are removed 7 — 10 days after surgery.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When should a wound culture be collected for a client with an infected wound?
questions.rationale: Antibiotics given first can prevent organisms from growing and give false results.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Skin cultures (PDF p. 447)
questions.quote: Obtain skin culture samples before first dose of antibiotic.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before swabbing a wound for culture, the nurse should first:
options: Rinse the wound with sterile saline
Use a cotton-tipped swab on pus
questions.rationale: Rinsing removes surface debris so the swab samples the wound bed; use a non-cotton swab.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Wound culture (PDF p. 447)
questions.quote: Rinse wound thoroughly with sterile normal saline. Use non cotton tipped swab.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should the nurse prepare a client for a Wood's light examination?
questions.rationale: The skin is viewed under ultraviolet light in a darkened room to find superficial infections.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Wood's light (PDF p. 447)
questions.quote: Darken the room prior to examination.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is scheduled for allergy skin testing. Which medication is usually stopped before the test?
questions.rationale: Antihistamines and systemic corticosteroids suppress the allergic response and cause false-negative results.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Skin testing (PDF p. 447)
questions.quote: These medications inhibit allergic response and will make results inaccurate.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which equipment must be ready during a scratch allergy test?
questions.rationale: The allergen may cause anaphylaxis, so resuscitation equipment and epinephrine must be available.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Skin testing (PDF p. 447)
questions.quote: Have resuscitation equipment available if scratch test is done, as it may induce anaphylactic reaction.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A farmer has a mole that has grown and changed color. The nurse recognizes this as a warning sign of:
questions.rationale: Change in color, size or shape of a lesion, or a sore that does not heal, are warning signs; UV exposure is the main cause.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Skin cancer (PDF p. 448)
questions.quote: Change in color, size or shape of preexisting lesion.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: To prevent skin cancer, a fisherman should be taught to:
options: Avoid midday sun and use sunscreen
Use oil to protect the skin
questions.rationale: Avoid sun from about 10 am to 3 pm, wear protective clothing and use sunscreen.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Skin cancer (PDF p. 448)
questions.quote: Wear layered clothing and use sun — screening lotions when outdoors.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has an itchy red rash with vesicles where a new watch strap touches the skin. The nurse applies:
questions.rationale: Contact dermatitis: cool wet dressings, cool environment, avoid the allergen, harsh soaps and heat.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Contact dermatitis (PDF p. 448)
questions.quote: Apply cool, wet dressings and tepid sponge bath as prescribed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has a red, warm, swollen, painful lower leg after a scratch. Which order does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Cellulitis is treated with rest, warm compresses, and antibiotics after culture.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Cellulitis (PDF p. 449)
questions.quote: Apply warm compresses 2 times per day to promote circulation and to decrease discomfort, erythema, and edema.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Raised red plaques covered with silvery-white scales on the elbows and knees suggest:
questions.rationale: Psoriasis is a chronic non-infectious disorder of rapid keratin turnover with silvery scales on extensor surfaces.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Psoriasis (PDF p. 450)
questions.quote: Shedding silvery, white scales on a raised, reddened, round plaque

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: New psoriatic plaques appear along a recent scratch on a client's arm. This is called:
questions.rationale: Koebner's phenomenon is the development of psoriatic lesions at a site of skin injury.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Psoriasis (PDF p. 450)
questions.quote: Koebner's phenomenon. It is the development of psoriatic lesions at a site of injury.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Purplish, raised oblong skin lesions in a client with advanced HIV suggest:
questions.rationale: Kaposi's sarcoma arises with immune failure, common in AIDS; punch biopsy confirms it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Kaposi's sarcoma (PDF p. 450)
questions.quote: This is common among clients with AIDS.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has painful vesicles in a band on one side of the chest. Who should avoid caring for him?
options: A nurse who never had chickenpox
questions.rationale: Herpes zoster lesions contain varicella-zoster virus and can cause chickenpox in non-immune people.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Herpes zoster (PDF p. 451)
questions.quote: Herpes zoster is contagious to individuals who have not had chicken pox.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which comfort measure helps a client with shingles?
questions.rationale: Warmth and touch worsen zoster pain; use a cool environment, bed cradle and light cotton clothes.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Herpes zoster (PDF p. 451)
questions.quote: Use an air mattress and a bed cradle on the client's bed, and keep environment cool. Warmth and touch aggravate pain.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a teenage girl starts isotretinoin for severe acne, the nurse ensures:
questions.rationale: Isotretinoin is teratogenic; pregnancy must be excluded and prevented. Also stop vitamin A and avoid sun.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Acne vulgaris (PDF p. 452)
questions.quote: Assess for pregnancy before starting Isotretinoin. Isotretinoin is teratogenic

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A teen with acne asks if he must stop eating chocolate. The nurse explains:
options: Food is not proven to cause acne
questions.rationale: Hormones, heat, humidity and sweating play a role; there is no evidence that chocolate or nuts cause acne.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Acne vulgaris (PDF p. 452)
questions.quote: There is no evidence that chocolate, nuts, fatty foods, or cosmetics affect acne.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which advice is correct for a client with acne?
questions.rationale: Don't squeeze, prick or scrub; use water-based cosmetics; improvement takes 4–6 weeks.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Acne vulgaris (PDF p. 453)
questions.quote: Instruct the client not to scrub the face; not to squeeze, prick or pick at lesions.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client says she gets itchy lips after eating banana and kiwi. The nurse should assess for:
questions.rationale: Allergy to banana, kiwi, avocado, chestnut and similar foods is linked with latex allergy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Latex allergy (PDF p. 453)
questions.quote: The client who has allergy to the following are at risk to develop latex allergy: kiwi, banana

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which item is safe to use for a client with latex allergy?
questions.rationale: Use latex-free items such as cotton pads, plastic or silk tape and vinyl or nitrile gloves.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Latex allergy (PDF p. 453)
questions.quote: If a client has latex allergy, use cotton pads, plastic or silk tape. These are latex — free products.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with scleroderma has fingers that turn white, then blue, in the cold. This is:
questions.rationale: Raynaud's is the R of CREST syndrome: vasospasm of the fingers with cold or stress.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Scleroderma (PDF p. 454)
questions.quote: R — aynaud's phenomenon

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Several villagers who butchered and ate a carabao that died suddenly now have painless skin ulcers with black centers. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Anthrax spreads by handling or eating infected animals, not person to person; skin lesions become painless black ulcers.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Anthrax (PDF p. 454)
questions.quote: The sac becomes a painless ulcer with an area of black, dead tissue in the middle.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A family asks whether anthrax spreads from a sick relative to them. The nurse explains that anthrax:
options: Is not spread person to person
questions.rationale: Anthrax is acquired from spores through skin, ingestion or inhalation; there is no person-to-person spread.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Anthrax (PDF p. 454)
questions.quote: There is no person-to-person contact.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with honey-colored crusted sores around the nose had impetigo. Which later complication should the nurse watch for?
questions.rationale: Impetigo from group A streptococci may be followed by post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (watch for tea-colored urine, edema).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 460)
questions.quote: Group A hemolytic streptococci can cause rheumatic fever and glomerulonephritis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client who started a new drug develops fever, painful purplish rash, blisters and peeling skin and mouth sores. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: SJS is a severe hypersensitivity reaction to drugs or infection; stop the drug and treat as an emergency.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Stevens-Johnson syndrome (PDF p. 454)
questions.quote: Skin and mucous membrane react to a medication or infection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which dressing is best for a wound with heavy drainage?
questions.rationale: Alginates absorb heavy drainage and protect the wound bed; films suit shallow wounds and hydrogels add moisture.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Moisture-retentive dressings (PDF p. 455)
questions.quote: Absorb heavy drainage and protect the wound bed

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When applying a wet-to-damp dressing to a deep wound, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Moist sterile gauze fills all crevices, then a dry dressing covers it; sterile gloves are used.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 13 Wet-to-damp dressing (PDF p. 455)
questions.quote: Pack all crevices and depressions in wound.
